messages:
amy_sales: hey team — Acme sent back the SIG asking specifically about BCP/DR, RTO/RPO, backups, failover, and uptime commitments. They want language we can include in the SIG response by EOD. Can someone draft tidy answers? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

rachel_se: I put together a concise set below that maps to typical SIG fields. Kept details high-level but actionable. Please flag anything we can’t commit to.

rachel_se: 1) RTO / RPO (summary):
- RTO (control plane): 1 hour for control plane services (user/project config, routing, deployments) under a regional outage with automated failover triggered.
- RTO (data plane/inference): automatic routing to healthy capacity with median failover impact < 15 minutes for supported multi-region customers. For single-region deployments, RTO depends on customer topology; can provide dedicated DR runbooks for Private/Dedicated customers.
- RPO: For customer-provided persistent data (object storage, model artifacts) we rely on S3-compatible storage with versioning and cross-region replication where configured — RPO is typically < 10 minutes for actively replicated objects. For ephemeral inference state (KV caches, GPU-local caches) RPO is best-effort; customers requiring tighter RPO should use persistent logging/hooks.

rachel_se: 2) Backups / snapshots / retention:
- Configuration and metadata: nightly immutable snapshots plus incremental replication; 30-day default retention (can extend per contract).
- Model/artifact storage: object versioning + optional cross-region replication; customers can bring their own storage and retention policies.
- Telemetry/Logs: 90-day hot retention by default in Console; longer retention via S3 export add-on.

rachel_se: 3) Failover and architecture:
- Hosted: active-active across multiple AZs, with cross-region failover configurable for enterprise accounts.
- Dedicated/Private: supports warm-standby & scheduled failover testing; deployment topology and exact RTO/RPO are scoped in onboarding/contract.
- BGP/edge routing + health checks ensure traffic is diverted to healthy regions and model variants when capacity constrained.

rachel_se: 4) SLA / uptime commitments:
- Hosted API: standard published SLA is 99.9% uptime for paid plans; higher SLAs (99.95%+) available on Dedicated/Enterprise contracts with capacity commitments and runbook integration.

rachel_se: 5) DR exercises and validation:
- We run quarterly DR tabletop exercises and annual live failover tests for enterprise customers (coordinated). Results and remediation items are tracked and shared in postmortems.

rachel_se: 6) Runbooks / playbooks / observability:
- We provide runbooks for common scenarios (region outage, partial capacity loss, degraded model performance) and postmortem templates.
- Console exposes per-route latency & error dashboards, trace links, and token-level cost breakdowns to speed triage.

leo_sec: few security caveats to add for SIG:
- All backups and replication streams are encrypted in transit and at rest using KMS-managed keys. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Private/Dedicated customers.
- Access to production backups is controlled via RBAC; all snapshot restores are audited.
- We have documented RTO/RPO acceptance criteria in our SOC2 controls map.

leo_sec: also recommend we include this short statement about limitations: "RTO/RPO for replicated customer-owned storage depends on customer-configured cross-region replication and the chosen Dedicated/Private topology. Ephemeral GPU-local state is not included in persistent backups."

amy_sales: this is great — can you paste a version formatted for the SIG (short answers, one-paragraph per question)? I need to paste into the CAIQ.

rachel_se: copying a compact SIG-ready block now:

rachel_se: ```
RTO/RPO: Redwood Inference operates an active-active multi-AZ architecture for hosted deployments and supports cross-region failover for enterprise accounts. Typical control-plane RTO is 1 hour; inference/data-plane failover for multi-region customers is usually <15 minutes. RPO depends on configured replication: with cross-region replication enabled we achieve sub-10 minute RPO for persistent artifacts. Ephemeral GPU-local caches are not persisted.

Backups & Retention: Configuration metadata is snapshotted nightly with 30-day default retention. Model artifacts and customer objects are stored in versioned object storage with optional cross-region replication; telemetry logs are retained 90 days by default with export options.

Failover & SLA: Hosted: active-active AZs and configurable cross-region failover. Dedicated/Private: warm-standby and runbook-driven failover options scoped at onboarding. Published hosted SLA: 99.9%; higher enterprise SLAs available with reserved capacity.

DR Validation: Quarterly tabletop exercises and annual live failover tests for enterprise customers; postmortems and remediation tracking are provided.

Security Controls: All backups are encrypted in transit and at rest with KMS; customer-managed keys are supported for enterprise/private deployments. Access to backups is RBAC-controlled and audited.
```

amy_sales: perfect. leo_sec are you ok with that security sentence?

leo_sec: yes, that’s acceptable as a high-level SIG reply. we should attach SOC2 and DR test cadence if they ask follow-ups. :+1:

ops-bot: scheduled DR-run-reminder for enterprise accounts posted to #eng-sre at 2026-04-01T16:00:00Z (auto).

amy_sales: awesome — I’ll send this back to Acme with a note that Dedicated/Private customers can get more prescriptive RTO/RPO commitments in contract language and onboarding docs. Thanks all. :rocket:
